newsitem.title: INDIA: Volkswagen said planning India car plant.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen said planning India car plant.

text.p: Germany's Volkswagen AG plans to invest $100 million in a car manufacturing plant in India, the Press Trust of India (PTI) on Monday quoted a senior Volkswagen official as saying.

PTI said Bernd Lohning told the news agency in the southern city of Bangalore that Volkswagen was seeking an Indian partner and hoped the factory would begin producing two models later this year. PTI did not give Lohning's title.
"We are looking forward to invest to the tune of about $100 million in India, and the plant would be in Bangalore," PTI quoted Lohning as saying.

Lohning said the project would be a joint venture with 50 percent of the equity held by an Indian car maker. "We have been talking to two leading Indian car manufacturers, and a decision on the final selection will be made in a couple of weeks," PTI quoted him as saying. He did not identify the car makers.
The Volkswagen official said the firm had visited sites around Bangalore.
The Germany car maker hopes that work on the Bangalore plant will begin by the middle of the year and production will start later in 1997, with delivery in 1998, he told PTI.

Last year Volkswagen said it was actively engaged with India's Eicher group, which makes tractors and light trucks, in identifying car models and the quantity to be built in India, as well as the location of new production facilities.
Eicher officials could not be reached for comment on Monday.

India's auto sector has already attracted major labels like U.S.-based Ford and General Motors, France's Peugeot and South Korea's Daewoo after opening its market under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
The companies have taken on Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp, which has been in India for more than a decade through its joint venture with the Indian government, Maruti Udyog Ltd.
Suzuki has a 70 percent share of the Indian car market.
Honda Motor Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Motor Corp are planning to start car production in India this year. Chrysler Corp and Fiat SpA are currently studying the feasibility of entering the Indian market.
